Hi everyone my name is Gabriel de Lima Monteiro, I'm a physicist with a PhD in applied math. I've just decided to finally give theorem-proving a try. I have a question regarding the structure of Mathlib.

I was searching for Schauder's fixed-point theorem which doesn't seem to exist in the mathlib doc. However, a google search returns the page https://lean-lang.org/eval/problems/schauder_fixed_point/ which points out that the formalization is done (by several users in fact).

Is there a way of using some of the submissions in order to be able to use Schauder's theorem ?

Submissions to lean-eval are in this repository:
https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Aleanprover%2Flean-eval-submissions+schauder_fixed_point&type=code
Out of the 7 submissions, only 1 chose to make it public:
https://gist.github.com/Morgan-Griffiths/9696b2ac9d473ab1f3a267a98507992e

That being said, if there were no source (and in this case the source is GPT generated) there wouldn't be a way to use the theorem, except to trust that comparator has done its job, and just write it as an axiom.
